text: India now has more than sixteen crore demat accounts, and most new investors come from Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns. Many of them learn about markets from WhatsApp forwards and YouTube finfluencers. Nirikshak helps them check before they trust. It audits a video, a forwarded tip, or a creator, and explains the risks in plain English or Hindi.

Let's start with the most common trap. Sunita receives this WhatsApp message. It claims her Zerodha account will be blocked, asks for an OTP, and wants a ninety-nine rupee fee. She pastes it into Nirikshak. She could also just drop in a screenshot.

In seconds, the verdict is clear: high risk. Every warning sign points to the exact line. The link pretends to be Zerodha but goes to a different website. The message asks for an OTP, and demands money on a UPI handle. And instead of a vague warning, Sunita gets three concrete steps: never share the OTP, don't pay, and contact the company through its official app, or call nineteen thirty.

Now a finfluencer video: three crypto coins that will make you a millionaire, with a hundred-x return guaranteed. Nirikshak read the whole transcript locally. Risk score: one hundred. The summary explains what the video is pitching, and the main concerns link straight to the moment they were said.

Then the most important question: who is giving this advice? Nirikshak checks every name, website and registration number against more than six thousand SEBI-registered entities. This creator is not registered as a research analyst or adviser, so he is not allowed to give buy or sell calls. There is also no risk disclaimer.

Every finding quotes the creator word for word, with the time, the category, how serious it is, and how confident the system is. Nothing is a black-box verdict: the user can always check the exact moment.
Users can also ask questions in their own words. Did he promise guaranteed returns? The answer comes only from what was actually said, with clickable timestamps as evidence.
But Nirikshak never gives investment advice. Asked whether to buy the coins, it declines, and instead points to what the video claimed and the creator's registration status.
Everything works in Hindi too. One tap switches the whole report, the explanations and the summary, and a natural voice can read it aloud for users who find reading hard.

One video can be an outlier, so Nirikshak can also profile a creator. All five of this channel's latest uploads are high risk. Every one pushes a paid Telegram group and makes confident price predictions, and two promise guaranteed returns. That pattern is the real warning.

Compare that with a SEBI-registered research analyst: registration verified, low risk across recent videos. Nirikshak is not against finfluencers. It helps people tell education and registered research apart from promotion.

Nirikshak never recommends stocks, shows its uncertainty openly, and its full version runs entirely on the user's own computer, so private messages never leave it. It is investor-protection infrastructure that any institution can run, in Hindi and English, for the next crore investors.
